CellChat parameters

Source: R/tool-cellchat.R
cellchatParam.Rd

Parameters for GiottoClass::analyzeData() that run CellChat (Jin et al. 2021) and its spatial mode from CellChat v2 (Jin et al. 2025), which infers cell-cell communication between cell groups from the expression of ligands, receptors and their cofactors (CellChatDB), with spatial distance between the groups as a constraint when coordinates are given. CellChat is an R package from GitHub, install it with remotes::install_github("jinworks/CellChat"). If you use it, please cite the original paper (see References).

Usage

cellchatParam(
  species = c("mouse", "human", "zebrafish"),
  db_search = NULL,
  non_protein = FALSE,
  type = c("triMean", "truncatedMean", "thresholdedMean", "median"),
  trim = 0.1,
  population_size = FALSE,
  variable_both = TRUE,
  thresh_p = 0.05,
  do_fast = NULL,
  nboot = 100L,
  seed = 1L,
  min_cells = 10L,
  thresh = 0.05,
  distance_use = TRUE,
  interaction_range = 250,
  scale_distance = 0.01,
  k_min = 10L,
  contact_dependent = TRUE,
  contact_range = 100,
  ratio = NULL,
  center_distance = NULL,
  tol = NULL,
  ...
)

# S4 method for class 'allMatrix,cellchatParam'
analyzeData(x, param, cell_type, spatial_locs = NULL, ...)

Arguments

species

CellChatDB to use: "mouse", "human" or "zebrafish"

db_search

CellChatDB annotations to keep (subsetDB()); NULL keeps all protein signaling ("Secreted Signaling", "ECM-Receptor", "Cell-Cell Contact"), CellChat's recommendation

non_protein

logical, also keep "Non-protein Signaling"

type, trim

how average expression per group is computed (CellChat's computeCommunProb(); "truncatedMean" with trim = 0.1 is less strict for low-depth spots)

population_size

logical, weigh by group sizes

variable_both

logical, require both ligand and receptor to be over-expressed (identifyOverExpressedInteractions())

thresh_p

p-value threshold for over-expressed genes

do_fast

logical, CellChat's fast Wilcoxon test, which needs the GitHub package presto; NULL uses it when presto is installed

nboot

integer, permutations for the p-values

seed

integer, seed of the permutations

min_cells

integer, minimum cells per group (filterCommunication())

thresh

p-value threshold of the returned interactions

distance_use

logical, spatial mode: use distance as a constraint

interaction_range

numeric, spatial mode: maximum interaction length in microns

scale_distance

numeric, spatial mode: distance scale factor

k_min

integer, spatial mode: minimum number of interacting cell pairs between two groups

contact_dependent

logical, spatial mode: run "Cell-Cell Contact" pairs only between touching groups

contact_range

numeric, spatial mode: contact distance in microns (about the cell diameter, or the spot distance for Visium)

ratio

microns per coordinate unit of the spatial locations; NULL derives it from center_distance

center_distance

microns between neighbouring centres (e.g. 100 for Visium spots); with ratio = NULL the ratio is center_distance divided by the median nearest-neighbour distance of the coordinates. One of ratio or center_distance is needed for the spatial mode

tol

tolerance in microns added to the ranges (CellChat uses half the spot or cell size, e.g. 32.5 for Visium); NULL uses half the median nearest-neighbour distance in microns

...

further options of computeCommunProb() as name = value

x

normalized (log) expression matrix, features x cells, feature names as gene symbols of species

param

a cellchatParam

cell_type

cell group of each column of x

spatial_locs

NULL (non-spatial mode) or a two-column matrix of coordinates, rows in the column order of x

Value

A cellchatParam object.

Details

analyzeData(x, param, cell_type, spatial_locs) returns a data.table with one row per significant interaction (source, target, ligand, receptor, prob, pval, interaction_name, pathway_name, annotation, ...; CellChat's subsetCommunication()). Its attributes are pathways (the pathway-level table), cellchat (the CellChat object, for CellChat's plotting functions) and spatial_factors (the ratio and tol used; NULL when non-spatial).

References

Jin S, Guerrero-Juarez CF, Zhang L, Chang I, Ramos R, Kuan CH, Myung P, Plikus MV, Nie Q. Inference and analysis of cell-cell communication using CellChat. Nature Communications 12, 1088 (2021). doi:10.1038/s41467-021-21246-9

Jin S, Plikus MV, Nie Q. CellChat for systematic analysis of cell-cell communication from single-cell transcriptomics. Nature Protocols 20, 180-219 (2025). doi:10.1038/s41596-024-01045-4

See also

runCellChat()

Examples

p <- cellchatParam(species = "mouse", center_distance = 100, tol = 32.5)
p$species
